ActivityDayRow.description: One local day's volume. Empty days are present, never trimmed.
ActivityDayRow.title: ActivityDayRow

ActivityHourRow.description:
One hour of the LOCAL day, summed across the window.

Asia/Tashkent, never UTC: "customers cannot get through at lunchtime" is
visible at 12:00 and becomes a meaningless 07:00 in UTC. Identical shape to
the daily row, because one chart draws both cuts.
ActivityHourRow.title: ActivityHourRow

ActivityResponse.description: The whole report: window, chart series, per-agent rows and the total.

callback_median_minutes.description: Company-wide median minutes to contact. Computed over calls, never as an average of the agents' medians — a median of medians ignores volume.

callback_window_hours.description: A later call counts as a callback only inside this many hours.

date_to.description: Inclusive: the last day the window covers.

total.description: The company row. Its customer counts are computed separately, not summed: one customer who called two employees is one person.

ActivityResponse.title: ActivityResponse

AgentActivityRow.description: One employee over the window. The company total uses the same shape.

callback_median_minutes.description: How long this employee keeps a customer waiting (median minutes). A different question from the rate: 100 % returned three hours later is a good rate and a bad service.

callback_rate.description: Reached as a percent of unreached customers, per CUSTOMER.

clients_unreached.description: THE HEADLINE: lost business, counted in people rather than calls.

inbound_total.description: Calls customers made to the employee.

missed.description: INCOMING and not answered — the company's responsibility, and the point of this report. `rejected` counts here with `missed`: the phone rang and there was no conversation.

missed_addressable.description: Missed events carrying a usable number. `missed_open` divides by this, because a number nobody has cannot be called back.

missed_clients.description: Distinct customers who could not get through; repeat attempts count once. Measured: 1.8 attempts per customer on average.

missed_rate.description: Missed as a percent of incoming. Null when there were none.

outbound_no_answer.description: The customer did not pick up. NOT a missed call and never added to one: measured over 7 days, 983 incoming unanswered against 1047 outgoing, so combining them doubles the figure and blames the employee for it.

outbound_total.description: Calls the employee made to customers.

AgentActivityRow.title: AgentActivityRow

AgentRankRowOut.description: One agent's standing over the window.

rank_delta.description: Places gained against the previous period; positive means moved up. Null for an agent who scored nothing in that period.

AgentRankRowOut.title: AgentRankRowOut

total.description: Agents with at least one scored call.

AlertKind.description:
Every cause that can raise an alert (SPEC §10.3).

SPEC §3.1 says "24 values"; §10.3's table groups the three
``permission_lost_*`` causes on one line and pairs
``retention_job_failed``/``backup_failed`` on another. Expanded, release 1's
closed set was the first 27 below — the count in §3.1 is a count of table
rows.

The last two arrive with the analysis module (SPEC-ANALYTICS §2.1, §5,
migration 011) and each exists because the nearest existing value would
point an admin at the wrong subsystem: a stalled AI pipeline raising
``retention_job_failed`` sends somebody to look at deletion, and a monthly
cap stopping the queue is not a failure at all — it is the safety rail
working, and it needs a name that says so.
AlertKind.title: AlertKind

AlertResponse.description: One open or acknowledged alert, as the inbox renders it.

body_uz.description: What to do about it. Derived from `kind`, not stored.

installation_status.description: Status of the installation this alert is about. New alerts are not raised against a superseded phone and its open ones are closed when it is replaced — this is here so a page can also tell at a glance, without a second query, for alerts raised before that rule existed.

occurrence_count.description: Repeats bump this rather than inserting a row: a phone reporting every two minutes must not produce 720 rows a day.

title_uz.description: What happened, in Uzbek. Derived from `kind`, not stored.

AlertResponse.title: AlertResponse

AnalysisCallHeader.description:
Which conversation this is (§7.4).

Carried in the analysis response on purpose: the detail page must say
*whose call, when, with whom and how long* without sending the reader to
the calls section to find out. The analysis section is a section of its own
(§7), so a link there is a navigation away from the page, not a tooltip.

``agent_name`` is resolved server-side for the same reason
``CallResponse`` resolves it — a name lookup per row in the browser is the
N+1 problem with a different owner.

call_type.description: Why a call was or was not scored: only `external` is scored, and `unknown` means the line directory cannot tell yet (§2.6).

remote_number.description: As the device saw it. NULL when the caller withheld it.

started_at.description: When the conversation happened. The list sorts on this (§7.3).

AnalysisCallHeader.title: AnalysisCallHeader

AnalysisFailure.description:
Why a call stopped. Closed, and ``NOT NULL`` whenever the stage is
``skipped`` or ``failed`` (a CHECK on ``call_analysis_state``).

``stage`` says whether the row is terminal; this says why. The three groups
below are not decoration — only the transient ones are re-queued by
``analysis_retry_transient``, and getting that membership wrong is how 885
rate-limited calls stayed permanently failed in BonviZvonki after the quota
they were waiting on had reset.
AnalysisFailure.title: AnalysisFailure

AnalysisFailureRow.description: One recent failure, with enough to act on it (§7.5).

stage.description: Which half was running: transcribe | score.

AnalysisFailureRow.title: AnalysisFailureRow

AnalysisListItem.description:
One row of the scored-call list (§7.3).

The columns §7.3 names and nothing more. No transcript text: a list of
fifty conversations is not a place to ship fifty transcripts, and the
detail page is one click away.

overall_score.description: NULL until the call is scored — a queued row still has a place in the list.

red_flag_types.description: Sorted and de-duplicated, for the chips. The quotes stay on the detail page: a customer's words do not belong in a list payload.

AnalysisListItem.title: AnalysisListItem

AnalysisListResponse.description: A cursor page of analysed calls, newest conversation first (§7.3).

total.description: Counted only when asked, exactly as /calls does it.

AnalysisListResponse.title: AnalysisListResponse

AnalysisMonthResponse.description:
This Tashkent calendar month's spend against the caps (§4.5, §11.1).

Tashkent and not UTC because the person reading the bill lives there: a
month turning over at 05:00 local would put the first five hours of every
month into the previous one's cap.

audio_minutes.description: Measured ASR input — the billing unit.

calls.description: State rows that reached `completed` this month.

cap_calls.description: The cap that actually protects the account until a price is entered, because an unpriced month can never reach the money one.

date_from.description: First day of the current Asia/Tashkent month. Named like every other window in this API; §6.2 sketched it as `from`, which is not a Python identifier.

priced.description: Whether any vendor price has been entered. **False is what stops the panel rendering $0.00 and implying the feature is free** — a cost of zero because nobody typed a price is not a free feature.

AnalysisMonthResponse.title: AnalysisMonthResponse

AnalysisStage.description:
Where one call stands in the analysis pipeline (SPEC-ANALYTICS §2.4).

The state row *is* the status: there is no ``calls.status`` column and
nothing on ``calls`` is written by the analysis module.

BonviZvonki's ``locked`` is deliberately absent. Locking is the claim query
(``FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED``) plus the worker's advisory lock, and neither
survives a crash — a persisted ``locked`` would, leaving a row that no
dispatch picks up and no operator can explain.
AnalysisStage.title: AnalysisStage

AnalysisStageCounts.description:
Calls per stage. One field per ``AnalysisStage`` member, always present.

A fixed object rather than a map, so a stage with nothing in it is a
visible zero instead of an absent key the panel has to default. The six
fields are pinned against the enum by a test.

skipped.description: **Not a failure** and the panel must not paint it as one (§2.4).

AnalysisStageCounts.title: AnalysisStageCounts

AnalysisStateResponse.description:
``call_analysis_state`` as the panel reads it (§6.2).

Also the whole answer to ``POST /analysis/calls/{id}``: queueing returns
the state and nothing else, so a first press and a re-press are
indistinguishable (§5's shape, applied to a panel write).

asr_calls.description: Requests that reached a provider, i.e. that cost money.

cost_micro_usd.description: Measured units x the admin-entered price. 0 also means **not priced** — see `AnalysisMonthResponse.priced` (§11.1).

failure_code.description: Why the call stopped. Present exactly when the stage is `failed` or `skipped` — a database CHECK, not a habit. The Uzbek headline is keyed off this in the panel's uz.json.

failure_detail.description: The provider's own message, redacted. Technical English beside the code, never the sentence a user reads.

failure_stage.description: `transcribe` or `score` — which half spent money before stopping.

AnalysisStateResponse.title: AnalysisStateResponse

AnalysisStatusResponse.description:
The operational view: what is waiting, what broke, what it cost (§7.5).

This is where an admin answers "why has nothing been scored since
Tuesday". It exists in phase 1 because without it that question has no
answer short of opening the database.

cooldowns.description: Only the roles currently sitting out; empty is the normal state.

not_analysable.description: Skips by reason, so '412 calls are waiting on the line directory' is visible rather than silent (§2.6).

recent_failures.description: Newest first, capped at 20 server-side. Not a paged list (§6.2).

waiting_retry.description: Failed on a transient code and inside the nightly retry's reach, so it will be tried again by itself. Separate from `stages.failed` on purpose: one of them needs a person and the other does not.

AnalysisStatusResponse.title: AnalysisStatusResponse

avg_duration_sec.description: Mean call length over the scored calls, rounded half up.

calls.description: **Scored** calls — the join to call_scores is an inner one. A call the pipeline skipped or has not reached is not in it; call_types below is what accounts for the difference.

calls_total.description: Every call in the window, scored or not.

compared_with.description: The window every delta_percent above is measured against.

red_flags.description: Scored calls carrying at least one red flag, not flags found.

filled.description: True when every period in the window is present, empty ones included. False past the 550-period ceiling, where only periods with data are returned — the panel then draws what it was given rather than pretending the axis is complete.

AnalyticsWindow.description:
The window a report was computed over, echoed back.

On every response, because five of the six are opened without naming a
window at all — the caller asked for "the last 30 days" and the page has to
be able to say which days those were.
AnalyticsWindow.title: AnalyticsWindow

AppVariant.description:
The ``targetSdk`` product flavour (D-06).

Reported on every heartbeat, stored on every call, so capture rate is
measurable per variant and not only per handset model.
AppVariant.title: AppVariant

signing_sha256_configured.description: Whether a signing fingerprint is configured. False means uploads are accepted without the key check — see docs/APK-SIGNING.md.

AppVersionResponse.description: One build in the distribution record.

created_by_name.description: Who uploaded it, resolved server-side. The id alone would make every page re-solve it through `GET /users`, which a manager cannot read — so a manager would see a bare uuid.

published_at.description: NULL means uploaded but not published — reaches nobody.

AppVersionResponse.title: AppVersionResponse

AssignmentListResponse.description: Full history for a number — this is the timeline the agent page renders.
AssignmentListResponse.title: AssignmentListResponse

AttestRequest.description:
``POST /api/v1/installations/{id}/attest`` (T142).

Attestation is deliberately weaker evidence than a proven binding, and the
reason is mandatory: an unexplained attestation is indistinguishable from a
mistake six months later.
AttestRequest.title: AttestRequest

AudioMissingReason.description:
Why a call has no audio. Closed, ``NOT NULL`` whenever audio is absent (N5).

UC-14 names six; SPEC §3.9 justifies the other four one by one. The gap
report's denominator excludes ``pending_upload`` and ``not_expected``,
which is what keeps "% of answered calls with audio" honest.
AudioMissingReason.title: AudioMissingReason

AuditAction.description:
Every auditable action (UC-24, N27).

SPEC §3.16 was written against this set after the fact and added two values
to it. Both earn their place by being separately *filterable*:

* ``retention_changed`` is technically a ``setting_updated``, but it is the
  one setting whose change destroys data — "who shortened retention, and
  when" must be one filter, not a JSONB dig through every settings change.
* ``command_issued`` is a person reaching into an employee's **personally
  owned** phone. It is the only action in the product that acts on somebody
  else's hardware, and this log is the only place that is visible.

Adding a value is a migration, which is the point: the list is closed so
that "everything that happened" is answerable from one column.
AuditAction.title: AuditAction

AuditResponse.description: One thing that happened. Immutable, by database trigger.

detail.description: Before/after values and counts. Never a password, a token or an enrolment code (N26). Open by nature — this is a server-side record, not a device payload, so §8's allow-list does not apply.

AuditResponse.title: AuditResponse

BlockBreakdownResponse.description:
The radar chart (BonviZvonki ``GET /analytics/blocks``).

A block the rubric does not name is **left out** rather than sent with a
null percentage: we do not know what to divide it by, and a bar with no
scale is worse than a missing one.
BlockBreakdownResponse.title: BlockBreakdownResponse

BlockScoreOut.description: One rubric block, averaged over the window.

block.description: The rubric's own key. An open vocabulary on purpose: scores are written under a pinned rubric_version, so a block a later rubric adds must still be readable. The panel renders an unknown key as the key.

max.description: From the rubric, never a second constant. The two were once typed separately, diverged 25 against 15, and the radar chart drew 106 % in front of a manager.

percent.description: score/max. The radar chart's axis, which is why it is bounded.

scored_calls.description: Calls this block's average is taken over.

BlockScoreOut.title: BlockScoreOut

CallAnalysisResponse.description:
Everything the detail page needs, in one request (§6.2, §7.4).

``state``, ``transcript`` and ``score`` are **independently nullable**. A
call the pipeline has never touched answers 200 with all three null — not
404, because the page must be able to tell "not analysed" from "no such
call", and only one of those two is worth an error.

``enabled`` is repeated here rather than left to ``/analysis/status`` for
the same reason: deciding what to render must not cost two round trips to
learn a boolean.

enabled.description: `analysis.enabled`. False plus a null state means the page says 'o'chirilgan' and offers no button — pressing it would 409 (§7.4).

CallAnalysisResponse.title: CallAnalysisResponse

CallAudioSummary.description:
What the call list and the detail page need to know about the audio.

``capture_route`` is here and not folded into "audio: yes/no" because
``S1-RECORDING.md`` is explicit that ``app_voice_recognition`` and
``app_mic`` must stay distinguishable: the per-model capture rate is the M0
baseline, and UC-23's regression alert compares against it. Collapsing the
routes would make "which mechanism actually works on this handset" an
unanswerable question.

available.description: Playable now — stored and not yet expired.

capture_route.description: Which strategy produced it (S1, M0, UC-23).

capture_route_detail.description: The folder name only, never a path from the phone.

duration_mismatch.description: The file's length disagrees with the call log (UC-14).

url.description: Path to stream from, present only when the recording is available. A path and never a signed or public URL (N20): the endpoint is token-protected, and the panel reaches it through the Service Worker bridge because a plain <audio src> cannot send an Authorization header (T153, N43).

CallAudioSummary.title: CallAudioSummary

CallDirection.description:
Ours, not BonviZvonki's ``inbound``/``outbound``.

The export (SPEC §4.9) maps ours onto theirs in exactly one place, so the
two vocabularies never leak into each other.
CallDirection.title: CallDirection

CallDisposition.description:
UC-11's five classes are direction x disposition.

``missed`` and ``rejected`` are incoming-only, ``no_answer`` is
outgoing-only — enforced by a CHECK, so the invalid combinations are
unrepresentable rather than merely unused.
CallDisposition.title: CallDisposition

CallListResponse.description:
A cursor page of calls (SPEC §4.0).

``total`` is computed only when the caller asks: a COUNT(*) over a filtered
500k table is affordable once per filter change and not once per page.
CallListResponse.title: CallListResponse

CallResponse.description:
A call as the panel reads it.

Carries the display fields, not only ids. Making the browser look up an
agent's name per row is the N+1 problem relocated to the client, and the
``device_model`` filter would otherwise exist server-side for a column the
panel cannot show.

agent_name.description: Resolved server-side; the panel renders it.

device_model.description: 'Xiaomi Redmi Note 12'. The device_model filter needs it.

number_e164.description: The registered line the call happened on.

CallResponse.title: CallResponse

CallSentiment.description: The model's reading of how the conversation went.
CallSentiment.title: CallSentiment

CallStatsBucket.description:
One point on the x-axis: UC-11's five classes, counted.

Every bucket in the window is returned, including the empty ones. A chart
that receives only the days something happened draws a straight line
through a silent week, which is the one thing this chart exists to show.

date_to.description: Inclusive, and equal to date_from for a daily bucket. The last bucket is clipped to today, so a part-month is not drawn as a whole one.

total.description: Every call in the bucket, which is what the same filter returns from /calls — not necessarily the sum of the five classes.

CallStatsBucket.title: CallStatsBucket

CallStatsResponse.description: ``GET /api/v1/calls/stats`` — the call flow the dashboard draws.
CallStatsResponse.title: CallStatsResponse

CallType.description:
Internal vs external (UC-25). ``unknown`` is the mandatory default.

An empty line directory yields ``unknown``, never ``external``:
BonviZvonki defaulted to external and 82 of 98 calls were mislabelled.
CallType.title: CallType

CallTypeCountsOut.description:
Calls by type, over the window. **Every key is always present.**

A fixed object rather than a map, so a type with nothing in it is a visible
zero instead of an absent key the panel defaults for itself — which is how
the two lists drift apart. The fields are pinned against ``CallType`` by a
test.

**Deliberately not narrowed to scored calls.** This is the breakdown that
explains the headline: the ``calls`` metric counts *scored* conversations,
and without this row a manager who sees "6" in a month of 22,000 calls
concludes the system lost the rest. Measured in BonviZvonki: 72 against
22,026 for the same period.
CallTypeCountsOut.title: CallTypeCountsOut

Capability.description:
One row per installation per capability (UC-03, §7.8).

Every one of these is verified by exercising it, never by reading a
permission flag — that is what makes ``granted_not_working`` expressible.
Capability.title: Capability

CapabilityState.description: ``granted_not_working`` is the OEM-permission-manager case UC-03 names.
CapabilityState.title: CapabilityState

CapabilityStateResponse.description:
One capability's current state, as the panel's matrix renders it.

A **required** capability the phone has never reported appears here as
``unknown`` with null timestamps, rather than being absent. Absence made
the page show every row green while ``capturing`` was false, with nothing
on screen saying which capability was missing — and a phone stuck part-way
through E2 is exactly that shape.

changed_at.description: Null until there is a state to have changed from.

checked_at.description: Null when this capability has never been checked.

CapabilityStateResponse.title: CapabilityStateResponse

CaptureRoute.description:
Which mechanism produced the recording (S1, the M0 baseline).

``NONE`` may only appear with ``has_audio = false``.
CaptureRoute.title: CaptureRoute

new_password.description: Minimum 10 characters and no other composition rule (SPEC §4.7): a rule people cannot follow is a rule they write on a sticky note.

CommandFailureReason.description: Why a command did not happen. UC-16 requires the panel to say which.
CommandFailureReason.title: CommandFailureReason

CommandKind.description: Server-to-device commands. No ``send_sms`` — SMS is out of scope.
CommandKind.title: CommandKind

latency_ms.description: acked_at - created_at, stored so UC-16's five-second bar is **measured** rather than assumed. R3 flags that bar as possibly unachievable on doze-restricted OEMs; this column is what turns that into a conversation with evidence.

CountMetricOut.description: A count, with its change against the previous period of equal length.

delta_percent.description: Percent change. Null when the previous period was zero or has no value — 'up from nothing' is not a percentage.

CountMetricOut.title: CountMetricOut

CreateAgentRequest.description: ``POST /api/v1/agents``. Creating an agent never creates a login.

employee_code.description: The roster import key; unique where set.

CreateAgentRequest.title: CreateAgentRequest

CreateAssignmentRequest.description: ``POST /api/v1/numbers/{id}/assignments`` — hand a line to an agent.

valid_from.description: Defaults to now. The period is [valid_from, valid_to).

valid_to.description: NULL means open-ended — they hold it now.

CreateAssignmentRequest.title: CreateAssignmentRequest

number.description: For kind='dial'. Named, not a free-form payload map (§8).

pattern.description: Digits to match. UC-25's '*700' is the suffix rule '700'.

CreateNumberRequest.description:
``POST /api/v1/numbers``.

The number is normalised to E.164 before it is stored, so the same line
typed three ways is one row — the uniqueness lives on the generated
``phone_key`` column, not on this string.

operator.description: beeline | ucell | mobiuz | uzmobile | other. A reporting axis (R19).

sim_owner.description: R10: which SIM relationships are not Bonvi's to keep.

CreateNumberRequest.title: CreateNumberRequest

agent_id.description: Required when role='sales' — it is what own-scope narrowing filters on, and the database has a CHECK saying so.

CurrentUserResponse.description:
``GET /api/v1/auth/me`` — what the panel's ``can()`` reads.

The permission list is resolved server-side and sent whole. The panel never
holds a role-to-permission map: a second copy of the matrix is a second
thing to forget to update.

agent_id.description: Set for a 'sales' account; what own-scope filters on.

must_change_password.description: The panel forces the change before anything else loads.

CurrentUserResponse.title: CurrentUserResponse

DataUsageRowOut.description: One installation's traffic against the cap the employee pays for.

over_cap.description: Past N14's cap: the app stops uploading audio over cellular.

DataUsageRowOut.title: DataUsageRowOut

DeviceDetailResponse.description: Device health plus its capability matrix (UC-17's device page).

bound_at.description: When this installation was bound to the number.

capabilities.description: Empty for a phone that has never reported — not missing.

capturing.description: UC-03's never-false-ready rule: every required capability working, a verified installation and a live service. One function computes it, so the phone and the panel cannot disagree.

created_at.description: When the row was created. With `installation_status` it is what distinguishes a live binding from one superseded an hour ago.

is_online.description: Derived, never stored: last_heartbeat_at is inside the alerts.device_offline_minutes window. Storing it would need a job to keep it false, and it would be wrong between runs.

never_reported.description: Bound and never sent a heartbeat. Kept distinct from ``is_online: false`` because the next action differs: never started is a person waiting for help right now; worked once and stopped is a phone in a lift or a battery manager to argue with.

ws_connected.description: Shown separately from is_online on purpose: a socket can be alive while capture is dead, and conflating the two is how a broken phone looks fine.

DeviceDetailResponse.title: DeviceDetailResponse

DeviceHealthResponse.description: Every UC-17 field, plus the identity the panel needs to name a person.

bound_at.description: When this installation was bound to the number.

capturing.description: Whether this phone is recording **right now**: every required capability working, the installation verified, the service alive (UC-03). Never null — a phone that has told us nothing is not recording, and a null here reads as 'no problem' to any check asking whether it is false.

created_at.description: When the row was created. With `installation_status` it is what distinguishes a live binding from one superseded an hour ago.

is_online.description: Derived, never stored: last_heartbeat_at is inside the alerts.device_offline_minutes window. Storing it would need a job to keep it false, and it would be wrong between runs.

never_reported.description: Bound and never sent a heartbeat. Kept distinct from ``is_online: false`` because the next action differs: never started is a person waiting for help right now; worked once and stopped is a phone in a lift or a battery manager to argue with.

ws_connected.description: Shown separately from is_online on purpose: a socket can be alive while capture is dead, and conflating the two is how a broken phone looks fine.

DeviceHealthResponse.title: DeviceHealthResponse

EnrolmentAttemptKind.description: ``step_timing`` carries the per-screen durations that make N40 measurable.
EnrolmentAttemptKind.title: EnrolmentAttemptKind

EnrolmentAttemptResponse.description: Where UC-01's failures appear, with timestamps.
EnrolmentAttemptResponse.title: EnrolmentAttemptResponse

EnrolmentCodeResponse.description: The code plus everything the admin has to pass on.
EnrolmentCodeResponse.title: EnrolmentCodeResponse

EnrolmentOutcome.description: Every way an enrolment step can end. The funnel's evidence base.
EnrolmentOutcome.title: EnrolmentOutcome

ErrorBody.description:
The body of every non-2xx answer (N35, SPEC §4.0).

A model rather than a fragment hand-written in the exporter, so the shape
clients generate against is the shape ``main.error_envelope`` builds.
``tests/test_conformance.py`` drives real requests through both.

code.description: The stable machine value. Clients branch on this.

message.description: Uzbek, for a person. Never branched on (§4.0).

request_id.description: Echoed from X-Request-Id; quote it in a bug report.

ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody

ErrorResponse.description: ``{"error": {...}}`` — the envelope itself, and the only error shape.
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

FunnelStage.description:
Where an agent is in the rollout (UC-17, SPEC §10.1).

``verified_by_admin`` is visibly distinct from ``number_verified`` because
attested is weaker evidence than proven, and the identity anchor must never
degrade silently (T142).
FunnelStage.title: FunnelStage

api_level.description: Part of the M0 baseline's identity.

app_variant.description: Capture rate is per variant, not only per model (D-06).

delta_pp.description: Below the threshold raises N4's alert.

GapByReasonOut.description: Why audio is missing, and how often. The closed enum, never free text.

counts_against_capture_rate.description: ``pending_upload`` and ``not_expected`` are excluded from the denominator: an unanswered call in it makes '% of answered calls with audio' meaningless (SPEC §3.9).

GapByReasonOut.title: GapByReasonOut

missing_total.description: Matches the filtered call list, because the same rows are counted.

status.description: Always 'ok' when the process is serving.

ImportAgentsRequest.description:
``POST /api/v1/agents/import`` — CSV text, not a file upload.

A one-off for ~33 people (T59), not a live integration. Text rather than a
multipart file because the realistic input is a paste out of a spreadsheet,
and asking somebody to save a file first is a step that fails.

dry_run.description: Default true, deliberately: the diff is shown before anything is written, because a roster import that half-succeeded is worse than one that did not run.

ImportAgentsRequest.title: ImportAgentsRequest

ImportRowResult.description: What would happen, or did happen, to one roster line.

reason.description: Why it was skipped or refused.

ImportRowResult.title: ImportRowResult

InstallationResponse.description: One installation, as the panel reads it.
InstallationResponse.title: InstallationResponse

InstallationStatus.description: Lifecycle of one app installation bound to one registered number.
InstallationStatus.title: InstallationStatus

email.description: The login identifier, matched verbatim against ``users.email``. Case-insensitive; the column is CITEXT.

LoginResponse.description: The user *and* their access token, so the panel needs one round trip.

agent_id.description: Set for a 'sales' account; what own-scope filters on.

must_change_password.description: The panel forces the change before anything else loads.

LoginResponse.title: LoginResponse

MissedClientRow.description:
One unreached customer — the detail that proves the number.

A row reading "15 missed, 100 % called back" looks wrong until this list
shows the 15 events came from 9 customers and every one was spoken to.

contact_inbound.description: True — the customer tried again and was answered; false — somebody called them back.

contact_name.description: Resolved on the handset from the employee's own contacts. Decoration, never identity — there is no customer catalogue.

contacted_by.description: Who spoke to them. May be a different employee.

MissedClientRow.title: MissedClientRow

NotAnalysableCount.description: One reason calls are being skipped, and how many (§7.5).
NotAnalysableCount.title: NotAnalysableCount

phone_key.description: Last 9 digits, generated by the database (N37).

OpenDeltaOut.description: A device whose own call-log count never reconciled (N3, §4.1 B).

subscription_unknown_count.description: Never folded into either side of the rate — the fail-closed rule made visible.

OpenDeltaOut.title: OpenDeltaOut

OutcomeSignalOut.description: What the conversation ended in, when it said so.

confidence.description: The model's own 0..1 confidence in this signal. A float inside a JSONB document, which §10's no-float rule is about columns.

OutcomeSignalOut.title: OutcomeSignalOut

PromptSection.description:
One named part of the assembled system prompt.

Sent with ``editable`` because the admin edits exactly one of them and has to
see the rest: without the surrounding context they repeat an instruction that
is already there (and pay for the tokens) or contradict it.
PromptSection.title: PromptSection

ProviderCooldownResponse.description:
A role sitting out a quota or an outage.

The first thing an operator needs when the queue goes quiet, which is why
the cooldown is a table and not a cache key with a TTL (§1.3).

reason_code.description: A daily quota and a 503 read very differently.

role.description: asr | llm. One cooldown per role.

ProviderCooldownResponse.title: ProviderCooldownResponse

PublicReleaseListResponse.description:
The current build of each variant. Empty before the first publish.

``total`` can only ever be 0, 1 or 2 — there are two variants — and it is
here anyway, because every list response in this API carries the same two
fields and a generated client that has to special-case one of them is worse
than a field that is always ``len(items)``.
PublicReleaseListResponse.title: PublicReleaseListResponse

PublicReleaseResponse.description:
One published build, as an anonymous visitor may see it.

A deliberately NARROW copy of :class:`AppVersionResponse` rather than a
reuse of it. That model carries ``created_by`` and ``created_by_name`` —
which member of staff uploaded the build — and a public page has no
business naming an employee. Widening this model is how that would happen
by accident, so it lists its fields rather than inheriting them.

Everything here is already public by another route: the bytes and their
SHA-256 come back from ``GET /api/v1/app/download/{version_code}``, which
SPEC §4.1 rule 5 makes public, and the version is printed inside the APK.

apk_sha256.description: So a download can be checked against what the server holds.

PublicReleaseResponse.title: PublicReleaseResponse

PublishRubricRequest.description:
`PUT /analysis/rubric` — **publish the next version**, never edit this one.

There is no update endpoint and no rubric id in this body, and that is the
design: the version that scored yesterday's calls has to stay exactly as it
was, or `call_scores.rubric_version` stops meaning anything.

description.description: Why it was published — the only place that reason survives.

extra_rules.description: Free text, added to the prompt of EVERY call, which is why it is capped: its length converts directly into money.

name.description: What to call this version. Required, and the server invents nothing: display text belongs to the panel's Uzbek catalogue (§14).

PublishRubricRequest.title: PublishRubricRequest

force.description: Clear the existing transcript and score so both are recomputed. **The only way to spend money twice on one call**, which is why it is a body field and not a query parameter somebody pastes.

ReadyResponse.description: Dependency readiness, one flag per dependency.

storage.description: The audio root exists and is writable.

ReadyResponse.title: ReadyResponse

ReceiverStatus.description: No heartbeat for 3 min -> degraded, 5 min -> down + a critical alert.
ReceiverStatus.title: ReceiverStatus

ReceiverStatusResponse.description:
The banner at the top of the rollout page (SPEC §9.4).

**If every receiver is down, nobody in the fleet can enrol**, so this is
the page's most important sentence and it says so before anyone tries. It
carries a real type for the same reason: an untyped body reaches the
contract as a free-form map, and the panel then has to parse defensively
exactly where it can least afford to guess.

active_receivers.description: More than one is a configuration change, not code.

callback_enabled.description: Is the callback route part of this deployment (`enrolment.callback_enabled`)? When false the panel says nothing about receivers: a route nobody installed is not an outage.

enrolment_possible.description: False means the rollout is stopped, not slow.

receiver_msisdn.description: The number screen E5 shows the agent.

receiver_name.description: Which gateway, for the admin to go and look at.

status.description: up | degraded | down. Down is 5 minutes without a heartbeat. Null when the callback route is not part of this deployment.

ReceiverStatusResponse.title: ReceiverStatusResponse

ReclassifyResponse.description: A directory change is only half done until the calls agree with it.

calls_reclassified.description: Calls whose call_type changed as a result of this edit.

ReclassifyResponse.title: ReclassifyResponse

total.description: Every occurrence counted, across all types.

RedFlagCountOut.description: One kind of breach, and how often it was found.

count.description: Occurrences, not calls — one call can carry the same type twice.

type.description: The rubric's key; open, like the block keys.

RedFlagCountOut.title: RedFlagCountOut

RedFlagOut.description:
One incident, with the evidence for it.

Every incident is returned, including repeats of one type: a manager
confirming an accusation needs the time and the quote of both. ``counted``
marks the one that actually moved the score — the penalty is charged once
per type, and the array's penalties sum to the total applied.

timestamp.description: '[MM:SS]' into the recording, when the model located it.

type.description: The rubric's red-flag key. A string and not a closed enum on purpose: the rubric is versioned (`rubric_version`) and phase 2 reads it from a row, so a score written under v1 must stay readable after v2 adds a flag. The panel renders an unknown key as the key.

RedFlagOut.title: RedFlagOut

RevokeResponse.description:
What was still queued when contact was lost.

Bonvi does not own the handset, so a revoke that claims a completed wipe
would be lying. ``revoke_confirmed_at`` stays NULL until the phone comes
back and says the local audio is gone.
RevokeResponse.title: RevokeResponse

RubricBlock.description: One block: a heading, a maximum, and the criteria that add up to it.

key.description: The key `call_scores.blocks` is keyed by. Changing it on a published rubric orphans the bars of every score written under the old one.

max.description: Block maximum. All blocks total exactly 100.

RubricBlock.title: RubricBlock

description.description: What earns the points; goes into the prompt verbatim.

id.description: Short key, e.g. `A2`. The model answers per criterion under it.

optional.description: Whether the model may mark this criterion `na` — not applicable to this conversation — and have it left out of the arithmetic entirely. **Defaults to false on purpose**: a criterion nobody thought about must be assessed, not quietly droppable. Most Bonvi customers are returning ones who state their order in a sentence; without this flag the full sales script is applied to a 30-second call and the employee scores 40 for doing everything right.

points.description: This criterion's own maximum. The block's criteria must sum to its `max`.

RubricPromptResponse.description:
What is actually sent to the model, assembled from the active rubric.

**Assembled by the server, never rebuilt in the panel.** Two copies of this
text would drift, and then the screen would show one prompt while the model
received another — a bug with no symptom.

approx_tokens.description: A rough count paid on every call: Uzbek and Russian run at roughly 3.3 characters per token. An order of magnitude, not an invoice.

extra_rules_limit.description: `prompt.MAX_EXTRA_RULES`, so the editor's counter cannot disagree with what the server accepts.

RubricPromptResponse.title: RubricPromptResponse

RubricRedFlag.description: One rule whose breach costs points, with the penalty it costs.

penalty.description: Negative, always: a red flag subtracts. Zero is legal and means 'record it, but do not charge for it'.

type.description: The key the model must answer with. `[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,31}` — checked again in the service, because a key the model cannot reproduce makes every answer fail validation and stops all scoring.

zeroes_score.description: Whether this flag takes the whole score to 0. The heaviest sanction in the product — swearing at a customer — and the panel never sets it on a NEW flag: one miscategorised rule would zero an employee's month.

RubricRedFlag.title: RubricRedFlag

RubricResponse.description: The active rubric, or a single version of it.

extra_rules.description: The admin's own instructions, appended to the prompt as a section of their own. Versioned with the rubric, so a score can say which instructions produced it.

extra_rules_limit.description: `prompt.MAX_EXTRA_RULES`. Sent with the rubric so the editor's counter cannot disagree with what the server accepts — BonviZvonki wrote the number into its page as well and had two copies of one limit.

id.description: NULL when nothing has been published and this is the pinned default.

label.description: `v3` — **exactly the string `call_scores.rubric_version` holds**, so a score can be traced back to the criteria that produced it.

stored.description: False means no row exists yet and this is `rubric_default.DEFAULT_RUBRIC`, which is what an unseeded database still scores with. The editor says so rather than pretending somebody published it.

RubricResponse.title: RubricResponse

RubricVersionListResponse.description: Every published version, newest first (SPEC §4.0's list shape).
RubricVersionListResponse.title: RubricVersionListResponse

RubricVersionSummary.description: One line of the version history. Nothing is ever deleted from it.
RubricVersionSummary.title: RubricVersionSummary

ScoreBucketOut.description: One ten-point band of the histogram.

ceiling.description: Inclusive. The top band is 90-100 rather than 90-99: a perfect score belongs in the highest bar, not in an eleventh one of its own.

ScoreBucketOut.title: ScoreBucketOut

ScoreDistributionResponse.description:
The histogram (BonviZvonki ``GET /analytics/distribution``).

Always ten bands, empty ones included — the same decision
:class:`CallTypeCountsOut` makes, and for the same reason: a histogram with
holes in it reads as a filter that ate rows.
ScoreDistributionResponse.title: ScoreDistributionResponse

ScoreMetricOut.description: An average score out of 100, to one decimal place.
ScoreMetricOut.title: ScoreMetricOut

ScoreResponse.description: One call's verdict and the evidence for it (§7.4's score block).

block_details.description: {blocks: {...evidence per criterion...}, meta: {...}} — how the number was reached, so 'why 78?' is answerable without paying to re-run. `meta.applicable_max` is what lets a header read '68 / 75' honestly when criteria did not apply (§7.4).

blocks.description: FLAT {block_key: points}, already normalised to the criteria that applied. **Never recomputed in the panel.** Keyed by the rubric's own block keys, so it is a map rather than four named fields: a rubric change must not need a server release to render.

cost_micro_usd.description: NULL while the price is unset — null means not priced, never free.

review_reasons.description: [{code, params}]. The panel renders the sentence from uz.json, so the column holds a machine reason and never display copy (§1.6).

rubric_version.description: Stamped per score: a rubric change never re-bases old numbers.

ScoreResponse.title: ScoreResponse

SetMinimumVersionRequest.description:
``PUT /api/v1/app/min-version``.

``acknowledged_stranded`` must equal the count the impact endpoint returns
right now. Not ceremony: it fails exactly when the number moved between
looking and deciding, which is when the admin's picture is stale.

acknowledged_stranded.description: The stranded count you just saw. Must still be true.

SetMinimumVersionRequest.title: SetMinimumVersionRequest

StoragePointOut.description: One day of the growth curve.
StoragePointOut.title: StoragePointOut

StorageReportResponse.description: N18: current usage, 30-day growth, and the projection it implies.

projected_bytes_12m.description: Today's total plus a year at the last 30 days' rate. The provision is 250 GB, and this is what says whether that is enough.

StorageReportResponse.title: StorageReportResponse

StrandedInstallationOut.description: One phone a proposed minimum version would refuse.
StrandedInstallationOut.title: StrandedInstallationOut

TimeseriesPointOut.description:
One period of the trend line.

``period_start`` and not BonviZvonki's ``date``: in the weekly bucket the
value is the Monday and in the monthly one the first of the month, so
"date" invites a reader to plot it as the day something happened.

ai_score.description: Null where nothing was scored in the period — a gap, not a zero.

period_start.description: The period's first day, in Asia/Tashkent (Monday for a week).

TimeseriesPointOut.title: TimeseriesPointOut

TranscriptQuality.description:
The model's own assessment of the transcript it was handed.

A column rather than a derived value because the review rule reads it: a
score computed from a transcript the model itself called ``low`` is one a
person should look at before it reaches an employee's average.
TranscriptQuality.title: TranscriptQuality

TranscriptResponse.description:
One call's transcript (§7.4's transcript block).

``audio_bytes`` and ``asr_ms`` are stored but not returned: they are cost
measurement (§11.1), they belong to the month's figures on the status page,
and a per-call byte count is not something the detail page renders.

language.description: What was asked of the provider, or NULL when it detected it.

text.description: Verbatim, in the '[MM:SS] SPEAKER_n: ...' form. The timestamps are not decoration — phase 2's click-a-line-to-seek reads them.

word_count.description: Real spoken words, service tokens stripped (`rules.count_words`). Stored so the review rule and the panel agree on one number.

TranscriptResponse.title: TranscriptResponse

UpdateNumberRequest.description: ``PATCH /api/v1/numbers/{id}``. The number itself is not editable.
UpdateNumberRequest.title: UpdateNumberRequest

UpdateSettingRequest.description:
``PUT /api/v1/settings``.

``confirm`` exists for one case: lowering the retention period below
``retention.confirm_below_months`` destroys recordings that still exist.
Without it the server changes nothing and returns 409 (SPEC §3.11).

confirm.description: Required when the change would delete data that still exists.

UpdateSettingRequest.title: UpdateSettingRequest

UpdateUserRequest.description: ``PATCH /api/v1/users/{id}``. Every field optional; absent means unchanged.
UpdateUserRequest.title: UpdateUserRequest

UploadReleaseResponse.description: What the upload found in the file, alongside the row it created.

signer_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the signing certificate, read from the APK's v2/v3 signing block. Compare it against docs/APK-SIGNING.md by eye if no fingerprint is configured yet — a build signed by another key cannot be installed as an update, only as an uninstall that destroys the phone's unsent queue.

signer_verified.description: True when it was checked against the configured fingerprint.

UploadReleaseResponse.title: UploadReleaseResponse

UserListResponse.description: A page of accounts. Small table, so no cursor: the panel shows them all.
UserListResponse.title: UserListResponse

UserResponse.description: A panel account. Never carries the hash.
UserResponse.title: UserResponse

UserRole.description:
A panel login's role (SPEC §3.2).

``service`` is deliberately absent: machine access is a ``service_tokens``
row, because a machine has no password, no session and no navigation. The
authorisation registry in ``core/permissions.py`` covers both and a test
asserts these three are a subset of it.

``viewer`` was removed on 2026-09-05 with the TV board — see
``core.permissions.Role``.
UserRole.title: UserRole

VerificationMethod.description:
How we proved the phone holds the registered number (UC-04, T142).

Ordered strongest to weakest, and the order is load-bearing: SPEC §9.3
requires the identity anchor to degrade visibly, so every place that
renders a binding renders which of these it rests on.

``self_declared`` is the weakest. It says only that whoever held the
single-use code an admin issued for this number typed it into this handset
— no line was proven. It exists because on this fleet the two proving
routes are frequently both unavailable: Uzbek SIMs leave
``getLine1Number()`` empty, and the callback route needs a receiver line.
Without it those handsets have no path to ``active`` at all, which is
strictly worse: an unenrolled phone reports nothing, so nobody can even see
that it is unverified. Governed by ``enrolment.allow_self_declared``.
VerificationMethod.title: VerificationMethod

VersionGateImpactResponse.description:
What raising the floor would cost, **before** it is raised (N34, UC-28).

These are personally owned handsets. A stranded phone drains its queue,
is then refused, and stays refused until somebody physically reaches that
salesperson — so this is not a preview of a config change, it is the cost
of a decision, and the panel shows it before the button.

unknown_version_count.description: Active phones that have never reported a version code. The gate lets these through, so they are not counted as stranded — but each one might be below the floor and we cannot say.

VersionGateImpactResponse.title: VersionGateImpactResponse

info.title: BonviCall panel API

get.description:
Who called whom, how many went unanswered, and who was called back.

⚠️ There is no single "unanswered" number. An unanswered INCOMING call is
the company failing to pick up; an unanswered OUTGOING call is a customer
who was busy. Measured over 7 days of real data: 983 and 1047. Adding them
doubles the figure, destroys its meaning and blames the employee for it.

A ``sales`` caller sees only their own row, and the ``agent_id`` filter in
the URL is ignored for them rather than merged.

422.description: Validation error, in the standard envelope

get.description:
Proves the number in the table, customer by customer.

⚠️ Same window and same logic as the summary — otherwise "9 in the table,
8 in the list" and nobody trusts either.

An agent this caller may not read is a 404, and so is an agent that does
not exist: the two answers are identical on purpose.

Validation error, in the standard envelope
Validation error, in the standard envelope

A one-off roster import, dry-run by default (T59).

~33 people, pasted out of a spreadsheet. The diff is shown before anything
is written, because a roster import that half-succeeded is harder to
recover from than one that did not run.

Severity, cause, agent, device, first/last seen and the repeat count.

``agent_id`` is what the agent's own card reads. The alerts page shows the
open list and nothing else since 2026-09-14 — an inbox that never empties
is an inbox nobody works — so one person's closed history is answered here
instead of by a second page.

get.description:
A cursor page, newest conversation first (§7.3).

Keyset and not offset, through the same ``cursor`` idiom as the calls list:
no row that existed when paging started is skipped or returned twice, which
an OFFSET cannot give while the pipeline keeps finishing calls underneath.

The sort is fixed at ``started_at DESC``. There is one ordering a reader of
this page wants — the newest conversation — and a sort control that can
disagree with the cursor is a way to lose rows for no gain.

422.description: Validation error, in the standard envelope

get.description:
One call's state, transcript and score, plus the call's own facts.

A call the pipeline has never touched answers 200 with all three null —
**not 404** — because the page must tell "not analysed" from "no such
call". A call belonging to another agent is the 404.

422.description: Validation error, in the standard envelope

post.description:
Queue one call; the worker picks it up within two minutes.

**Never runs a provider call inside the request.** An LLM round trip behind
an HTTP request is how a panel times out and a user presses the button
again — and each press would be a second bill.

Returns 200 with the state row whether it was created or already there, so
a re-press is indistinguishable from the first press. The four ways this
answers 409 — the feature is off, the call is not analysable, the month's
cap is reached, no provider is configured — are decided in the service.

422.description: Validation error, in the standard envelope

get.description:
The rubric new scores are produced against.

Answers 200 even when nothing has been published: the response is then the
rubric pinned in ``rubric_default.py`` with ``stored: false``, which is
exactly what such a database scores with. Reading does **not** create the
row — BonviZvonki's version did, which made this GET a write.

put.description:
Publish the next version and make it active.

422 ``validation_error`` with a ``reason`` in the detail when the rubric
cannot produce a comparable score — the blocks not totalling 100 is the
first of those reasons, and the rubric is **not saved**.

422.description: Validation error, in the standard envelope

get.description:
What is actually sent to the model, assembled from the active rubric.

Read-only, and the sections say which single one is editable. An admin who
cannot see this text edits blind; an admin who could edit all of it could
break the response format and stop every score from validating.

Every published version, newest first.

Not paged: a rubric is published a handful of times a year, and the history
is the audit trail of "who changed how people are scored, and when" — which
is worth reading whole.

post.description:
Go back to an earlier version — the undo for a bad edit.

The version keeps its own number rather than being re-published under a new
one, so scores written before and after the round trip carry the same label
and really were produced by the same criteria.

422.description: Validation error, in the standard envelope

get.description:
What is waiting, what broke, and what the month has cost (§7.5).

Declared **above** ``/calls/{call_id}``: the two do not collide, but the
literal route staying above the parameterised one is the habit that keeps
them from colliding the day a path is renamed.

Not paged. ``recent_failures`` is capped at twenty server-side, and none of
the four fields below it is a list of rows to walk (§6.2).
Agents by average score, with the places gained since the last period.

get.description:
The APK itself. **Public** (SPEC §4.1 rule 5), rate-limited.

The install landing page sends a salesperson's browser here and that
browser has no session. The binary is a client and holds no secret; the
enrolment code is the secret, and it guards the page that links here.

``variant`` is what makes the answer unambiguous: both flavours of one
release carry the same ``version_code`` (SPEC §7.2), so the code alone
named two files and the caller got whichever the database returned first.
Omitted, it hands out ``legacy28`` — the fleet's build, and the one that
installs on every supported Android.

422.description: Validation error, in the standard envelope

get.description:
The current published build of each variant. **Public**, rate-limited.

What the site's front page reads, so that somebody sent to this server can
install the app without an account. It is the same permission decision SPEC
§4.1 rule 5 already made for the APK itself: the binary is a client and
holds no secret, and a version number beside it tells an attacker nothing
the file would not.

It answers an EMPTY list before the first publish, and that is a real
answer rather than a 404 — a fresh server has no build, and the page says
so in Uzbek instead of offering a button that goes nowhere.

``PublicReleaseResponse`` is a narrow model on purpose: the admin-facing
one names the member of staff who uploaded the build.

put.description:
Raise or lower the floor, having stated what it costs.

409 ``stranded_count_mismatch`` when the number moved since the impact was
read. That is not pedantry — it is the case where the admin is deciding
against a picture that is no longer true.

422.description: Validation error, in the standard envelope

get.description:
Who a proposed minimum would strand — read this before changing it.

Deliberately a ``GET`` with the candidate in the query string, so it can be
called repeatedly while an admin tries numbers, and so the panel can show
the cost live beside the input rather than after the fact.

422.description: Validation error, in the standard envelope

get.description: Every build, newest first. Both variants — they ship in lockstep.

post.description:
Store a build. **Uploaded is not published** — this reaches nobody yet.

``multipart/form-data`` rather than the JSON everything else uses, because
the payload is a binary the admin picked in a file dialog. It is the only
such endpoint in the product.

Take back a build that reached nobody.

Unpublished only. A published build stays: it is the distribution record,
and a phone may be downloading it right now. This exists because an upload
with a mistyped version code would otherwise hold that code for ever — the
unique constraint refuses the corrected re-upload.

Public, rate-limited. A wrong e-mail and a wrong password give the same answer.

Two windows, both SPEC §4.0 and both counting **failures only**

A cursor page. Default and guaranteed-stable sort is ``received_at DESC``.

Keyset, not offset: no row that existed when paging started is skipped or
returned twice, which is what UC-19 asks for and what an OFFSET cannot give
while calls keep arriving. **Every sort pairs with ``id``**, or paging
duplicates the rows whose sort values tie — and duration ties constantly.

422.description: Validation error, in the standard envelope

get.description:
The recordings of **the page the reader is looking at**, as one ZIP.

Deliberately a page and not a filter. The button sits under fifty rows and
hands over those fifty rows; "everything since January" is a different
product decision, and one whose size nobody can see before pressing it.
It therefore takes the same ``cursor``, ``limit`` and sort as the list, so
the archive and the screen cannot disagree about which calls they mean.

``limit`` is clamped exactly as the list clamps it, so hand-editing the URL
widens nothing.

Every recording it contains is one this principal may already download one
at a time: the page comes from the same scoped query, so own-scope means
own recordings. **One audit row per archive**, not one per file — the
question this action answers is "who took a copy, and of what", and seven
hundred rows would bury the log the way open alerts once buried the alerts
page.

422.description: Validation error, in the standard envelope

get.description:
Streaming CSV for the same filter as the list (T48, UC-22).

UTF-8 **with a BOM** and a ``;`` delimiter: Excel in a ru/uz locale renders
a comma-separated UTF-8 file as one column, and the person who opens it has
no way to know that is what happened.

A ``sales`` export is own-rows-only and carries no other agent's name,
because the same scoped query builds it.

422.description: Validation error, in the standard envelope

get.description:
Calls per day (or per month) per class, for the dashboard's chart.

Declared **above** ``/{call_id}``: that route takes a UUID, so a request
for ``/calls/stats`` matched against it answers 422 rather than reaching
this one.

A preset window is the server's arithmetic and not the caller's — the
browser asking for "a year" in its own timezone would draw a chart whose
edges disagree with every other date in the product (D-10) — so
``date_from``/``date_to`` are read only for ``period=custom``, and both are
required there. The granularity of a custom range is derived from its span,
not chosen: two dates are the question, and a second control before an
answer is one decision too many.

Own-scope applies exactly as it does to the list, because it is the same
query.

422.description: Validation error, in the standard envelope

delete.description:
**405 for every role, including admin** (UC-26, T45).

The route exists precisely so that the refusal is explicit and testable.
Without it a DELETE would 405 from the router with FastAPI's own body, and
"nobody can delete a call" would be an absence rather than a decision.
Only the retention job removes audio, and it never removes a call.

**No permission dependency on purpose.** T45 asserts 405 for all five
roles, so the refusal has to outrank authorisation: a role that cannot read
calls getting 403 here would mean the answer depends on who is asking, and
it does not.
A caller with no token still gets 401 — that is the principal dependency.
